episodes.title: The trial for the soul of the Indian Constitution.

blocks.text:
1970–1973. Prime Minister Indira Gandhi’s government passed constitutional amendments claiming unlimited power: Parliament could amend, repeal, or rewrite ANY part of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights.

One seer and one legendary lawyer stood in their way.

FACTUAL MATRIX (Statement of Facts): 1970–1973. Prime Minister Indira Gandhi’s government passed constitutional amendments claiming unlimited power: Parliament could amend, repeal, or rewrite ANY part of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights.

One seer and one legendary lawyer stood in their way. The legal controversy originated from whether the act committed fell within the statutory exceptions.

episodes.title: 24 April 1973: The 703-Page Judgment that Saved India.

blocks.text:
On 24 April 1973 (the day before CJI Sikri retired), the Supreme Court delivered 11 separate opinions totaling 703 pages.

By a razor-thin 7–6 majority, the court ruled:
**Parliament has wide power to amend the Constitution, but it CANNOT alter its Basic Structure.**

Swami Kesavananda Bharati lost his land petition, but his name became immortalized as the case that saved Indian democracy.

episodes.title: The Golden Precedent that Stopped Dictatorship.

blocks.text:
During the 1975 Emergency, the government passed the 39th Amendment to make Prime Minister election unchallengeable in any court.

The Supreme Court used the Basic Structure Doctrine to strike it down, declaring Judicial Review and Free Elections part of the untouchable Basic Structure.

Today, India’s democracy stands protected because no government can ever rewrite the foundational pillars of the republic.

episodes.title: 24 अप्रैल 1973: 703 पन्नों का वह फैसला जिसने भारत को बचाया।

blocks.text:
24 अप्रैल 1973 को (सीजेआई सीकरी के रिटायरमेंट से ठीक एक दिन पहले) सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने 11 अलग-अलग रायों के साथ 703 पन्नों का फैसला सुनाया।

7-6 के बहुमत से कोर्ट ने तय किया:
**संसद के पास संविधान संशोधन की व्यापक शक्ति है, लेकिन वह इसके बुनियादी ढांचे को नहीं बदल सकती।**

स्वामी केशवानंद भारती अपनी जमीन का केस हार गए, लेकिन उनका नाम भारतीय लोकतंत्र को बचाने वाले सबसे बड़े मुकदमे के रूप में अमर हो गया।

episodes.title: वह नजीर जिसने तानाशाही को रोका।

blocks.text:
1975 के आपातकाल के दौरान सरकार ने 39वां संशोधन पारित कर प्रधानमंत्री के चुनाव को किसी भी अदालत में चुनौती से परे कर दिया था।

सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने बेसिक स्ट्रक्चर सिद्धांत का उपयोग करके इस संशोधन को रद्द कर दिया और न्यायिक समीक्षा तथा निष्पक्ष चुनाव को संविधान का बुनियादी ढांचा घोषित किया।

आज भारतीय लोकतंत्र सुरक्षित है क्योंकि कोई भी सरकार कभी भी संविधान के मूल स्तंभों को मिटा नहीं सकती।

flashcards.q: Which court decided Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala and in what year?
flashcards.a: Supreme Court of India in the year 1973.

flashcards.q: What was the primary legal issue addressed in this case?
What is the core Ratio Decidendi of the judgment?
flashcards.a: In a 7-6 majority verdict, the 13-judge bench held that Parliament has wide power to amend any part of the Constitution, but CANNOT alter or destroy its "Basic Structure".

flashcards.q: What is the primary citation for this ruling?
flashcards.a: Kesavananda Bharati Sripadagalvaru v. State of Kerala, (1973) 4 SCC 225, AIR 1973 SC 1461

flashcards.q: What is the current legal status of this precedent?
flashcards.a: Basic Structure Doctrine remains the cornerstone of Indian constitutional review.

timeline.event: 13-judge bench rules Parliament cannot alter or destroy the Basic Structure of Constitution.
Applied in Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain to invalidate 39th Amendment.
Reaffirmed in Minerva Mills v. Union of India.

subsequentHistory.note: Affirmed and applied in subsequent landmark jurisprudence.
